faults.quote: I don't have split of revenue decline between passengers and average fare.
faults.why: The ledger answers this at least coarsely: same flights, same fleet and a flat load factor mean passengers were flat, so the whole decline is fare. The candidate pieced this together from later releases.

faults.quote: There have been no material changes to wages or other costs per flight. Fixed costs — aircraft leases, hub facilities and corporate overhead — were $20.0M in both FY2023 and FY2025.
faults.why: The candidate asked for a cost breakdown by major category for both years. Only a qualitative per-flight line and the fixed-cost total were given, with no 'I don't have' for the category split.

faults.quote: I'll come back to ancillary revenue per passenger shortly.
faults.why: The candidate asked for average fare per passenger in FY2023 vs FY2025. Only the ancillary part was deferred; the fare ask got no word at all.

faults.quote: Across all six routes, revenue fell from $200.0M to $176.0M and contribution fell from $40.0M to $16.0M, on 14,000 flights a year
faults.why: The network totals were released in answer to a fare and ancillary-per-passenger ask they don't answer.
The candidate misquoted fixed costs as $21M (the interviewer gave $20M). No flat correction ever came; the code held it and never released it.

faults.quote: On the flights assumption: you said the number of flights is roughly the same. Is that something you've been given, or are you assuming it? What would you need to confirm it?
faults.why: The data line in the same turn had just confirmed the flights were the same, which makes the probe moot. It is also three questions stacked in one turn.

faults.quote: On extras revenue per passenger and Hub–Lakeport's seats and load factor: we'll get there in a bit.
faults.why: This defers extras revenue per passenger in the same turn that just stated '$20 of extras per passenger', which contradicts itself.

faults.quote: The low-cost airline's cost per seat is about 30% lower than Larkspur's — it flies larger planes and has lower labor costs
faults.why: The candidate asked for the competitor's seat count per flight. Only 'larger planes' was given, with no 'I don't have the seat count'.

faults.quote: About 20% of passengers on the two contested routes are connecting at the hub to another Larkspur flight.
faults.why: The candidate asked for evidence behind demand on the new routes. Connecting share on the contested routes is a different entity, and there was no refusal for new-route traffic data.

faults.quote: Where did that figure come from, and how does it line up with the planning estimate for those routes?
faults.why: 'That figure' dangles after two unrelated data sentences. The $8,800 misquote of an exhibit figure was also probed rather than flatly corrected.

faults.quote: As I mentioned: About 20% of passengers on the two contested routes are connecting at the hub to another Larkspur flight. As the exhibit shows: On the other four routes revenue and contribution stayed nearly flat
faults.why: The candidate asked for revenue attributable to connecting passengers on onward legs. Lines already out were repeated instead, with no refusal, so the ask went unanswered.

faults.quote: On the price elasticity of those four routes, I'll check what we have.
faults.why: The elasticity ask was never resolved later: no release, no refusal, no 'we won't get to it'.

faults.quote: Repeating what I said before: On the other four routes revenue and contribution stayed nearly flat
faults.why: The route results line was restated for the second turn running, in answer to an elasticity ask it doesn't answer.

faults.quote: Hub–Westhaven (2,000 flights) held at $24.8M of revenue and $3.8M of contribution.
faults.why: The candidate misquoted Westhaven contribution as $3.6M (it is $3.8M) at t23, t29 and t31. No flat correction ever came, only a buried restatement.

faults.quote: Earlier you mentioned the redeployment swings us by about $13.8M. Can you walk me through the components of that figure?
faults.why: The candidate had already redone the inputs at t21 ($2,000 per flight, $10M), so the $13.8M figure was superseded. The candidate said as much: 'That figure is stale'.

faults.quote: What's the very first thing you'd have the client do?
faults.why: The candidate's mitigation answer had just led with 'validate demand before committing', which already covered the first step.
